description:
Before `fz-rh2.29.3` cuts the seal over from the monolith to `RuntimeDemand(E)` facts, prove equivalence at the consumer boundary instead of comparing raw internal demand maps.

## Fear
Raw `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` equality is the wrong assertion: it pressures `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)` to imitate the monolith trace, including local value/call-arg provenance and scheduling artifacts. But simply checking fact presence is not enough for cutover; the fact path could be complete and still project a different transport plan.

## Goal
Add a transport-projection equivalence check that derives the transport-facing obligations from both sources and proves they match where codegen/materialization consumes them.

## Strategy
- Keep `settle_runtime_demands` authoritative until this proof exists.
- Build or extract a projection helper that can compare monolith runtime demands with shadow `RuntimeDemand(E)` facts at the transport plan/shape/callable-publication boundary.
- Treat conservative internal provenance differences as acceptable only when the projected transport obligations are identical or intentionally equivalent by a documented relation.
- Do not add root-wide runtime-demand scans or a mini monolith inside `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)`.

## Check
Focused runtime-demand tests and the compiler2/fixture matrix pass with the transport-boundary equivalence check enabled. `fz-rh2.29.3` remains blocked until this passes.
title: Runtime demand: prove shadow fact equivalence at transport projection
